newsitem.title: GERMANY: DAG union says calls strike ballot at Lufthansa.
newsitem.headline: DAG union says calls strike ballot at Lufthansa.

text.p: The DAG white collar workers' union said it had decided to call a strike ballot at German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG in a dispute over pay at the airline.
The DAG has already staged two limited walk-outs over the issue. If a full strike is to go ahead, it will need to get the support of 70 percent of its members at the airline.

The DAG said in a statement that the ballot would take place over the next three or four weeks, balloting ground and air crews as well as pilots.
The lengthy ballot period was intended to allow flight crews who travelled abroad to participate in the vote.
The DAG said it hoped its action would convince Lufthansa to make a one-year pay agreement offering a pay rise in line with others in the sector.
DAG deputy chairman Hubert Gartz said that his union was not prepared to accept a pay agreement running over 27 months as sought by the airline.

Lufthansa has offered a one-off payment of 33 percent of a monthly salary to cover the first 1-1/2 years of the proposed contract followed by a 1.7 percent pay rise. The union is seeking a four percent pay increase.
